property_summary: For any caller, the function approvedToLog returns true if and only if the caller is approved by the owner.
After any call(s), approvedToLog for any address must equal its stored mapping value.
Setting a logger's approval status should affect the mapping at the specified address, not always the zero address.
After any sequence of calls, approvedLoggers[address] remains unchanged when address is not the owner and no setApprovedLogger call targeted that address.
For any address previously set as an approved logger, calling approvedToLog on that address returns true unless it has been explicitly revoked.
The value of approvedLoggers at address(0) is never changed by calling setApprovedLogger with any non-zero address.
For any address, after a sequence of calls, approvedLoggers at that address equals the status last set for that same address by setApprovedLogger.
After any sequence of calls, including setApprovedLogger, the mapping approvedLoggers remains unchanged for the key that was passed to setApprovedLogger.
After any call to setApprovedLogger with any address and status, the value of approvedLoggers for that address is the status that was passed.
After any call to setApprovedLogger, approvedLoggers mapping is unchanged for any address.
After any sequence of calls, the mapping `approvedLoggers` is never updated when `setApprovedLogger` is called.
For any address, calling setApprovedLogger with that address and true makes approvedToLog return true for that address.
For any caller and any address, the return value of approvedToLog must equal the stored mapping value for that address after the last setApprovedLogger call.

After any call to setApprovedLogger(address, bool) by the owner, the return value of approvedToLog(address) for any address equals the bool argument passed to setApprovedLogger, unless the caller is not the owner (revert).

For any caller and any address, approvedToLog must return the same value for that address after either a setApprovedLogger call with false or no setApprovedLogger call at all, but the bug always returns true.

After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger with any argument, approvedToLog must return false for any address that was previously set to false or never set, but the mutant always returns true for such addresses.
After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger(address, false) for some address, approvedToLog for that address must return false, but the mutant always returns true.
After setting a logger's approval status to false, that logger is no longer approved.
After calling setApprovedLogger with any address and any status, that address's approval status in approvedLoggers is unchanged if the caller is not the owner.
The approvedLoggers mapping reflects the last setApprovedLogger call; setting an address to true makes it approved, setting it to false makes it not approved, regardless of previous state.

After any call to setApprovedLogger with _status = true, the corresponding address becomes approved (approvedLoggers returns true); with _status = false, it becomes not approved (approvedLoggers returns false).
Setting any address to approved (true) makes it approved; setting it to not approved (false) makes it not approved.
For any caller and any key, after calling approvedToLog(key), the state of approvedLoggers is unchanged.
Only the owner can change the approvedLoggers mapping via setApprovedLogger.
After any call to approvedToLog, the approvedLoggers mapping remains unchanged.
Only the owner can successfully call setApprovedLogger to change the approvedLoggers mapping.
Only the owner can modify the approvedLoggers mapping via setApprovedLogger.
The owner cannot change the mapping approvedLoggers because onlyOwner modifier always reverts for the buggy contract.
Any address can become an approved logger by calling setApprovedLogger on itself if the caller is the owner.
The approvedLoggers mapping can only be changed by the owner via setApprovedLogger in the reference, but in the buggy version it can never be changed.
For any caller that is an approved logger, logCreated returns true.
For any address that is not an approved logger, logCreated returns false before emitting the event.
The return value of logCreated equals msg.sender's approval status as given by approvedToLog, i.e., logCreated returns true if and only if the caller is approved.
For any address that is an approved logger, calling logCreated returns true.
Calling logCreated on behalf of a non-approved logger never returns true.
logRedemptionRequested returns false when and only when the caller is approved to log
logRedemptionRequested returns true when and only when the caller is not approved to log
logRedemptionRequested returns false when and only when the caller is approved to log
For any approved logger, logGotRedemptionSignature returns true; for any unapproved logger, it returns false.
The return value of logGotRedemptionSignature equals the negation of the boolean from approvedToLog for the caller.
The return value of logGotRedemptionSignature equals approvedToLog for the caller after calling setApprovedLogger with the caller
For any caller, the boolean return value of logGotRedemptionSignature equals the negation of the boolean return value of approvedToLog for that caller.
For any approved logger, logGotRedemptionSignature returns false, and for any unapproved logger, it returns true.
logGotRedemptionSignature returns true when caller is approved and call succeeds
After a successful logGotRedemptionSignature call by an approved caller, the return value is true
logGotRedemptionSignature returns true when caller is approved and all parameters are arbitrary bytes32 values
logGotRedemptionSignature returns the opposite of the internal success indicator when caller is approved.
For any caller, if logGotRedemptionSignature returns true, then a subsequent call to approvedToLog with the same caller must return true.
The logRegisteredPubkey function returns true exactly when msg.sender is an approved logger.
The logRegisteredPubkey function returns true if and only if msg.sender is NOT an approved logger.
After a call to logRegisteredPubkey() that returns false, the event RegisteredPubkey is not emitted.
The return value of logRegisteredPubkey is true exactly when the caller is NOT an approved logger.
logRegisteredPubkey returns true exactly when the caller is NOT an approved logger.
For approved callers, the return value of logSetupFailed is always true.
When the caller is an approved logger, logSetupFailed() returns true; otherwise it returns false.
For any call to logSetupFailed() by an approved logger, the function returns true; for any call by a non-approved logger, it returns false.
For any call to logSetupFailed() that does not revert, the function return value must be true if and only if the caller is an approved logger.
For any call to logSetupFailed() that does not revert, the function returns true if and only if the caller is an approved logger.
logFunded returns true if and only if msg.sender is approved to log.
logFunded returns true if and only if the caller is approved to log.
After calling logFunded, the return value of approvedToLog for the caller remains the same as before the call.
logFunded returns exactly the same boolean as approvedToLog for the caller immediately after the call.
logFunded returns the same value as approvedToLog(msg.sender) before the call, for any caller.
The return value of logCourtesyCalled() is true if and only if the caller is approved to log.
The return value of logCourtesyCalled() is false if and only if the caller is approved to log.
After calling logCourtesyCalled() with the contract owner as msg.sender, the return value of approvedToLog(owner) remains unchanged.
The return value of logCourtesyCalled() equals the negation of approvedToLog(msg.sender) when called by a non-owner.
The return value of logCourtesyCalled() is always true when msg.sender is an approved logger.
